trainers.instruction: Select the correct word or words.

atoms.a: In which habitat do these animals live?
Which words describe the rainforest habitat best?

atoms.b: Rainforests are home to ((++many almost_no)) animals and plants.
In fact, scientists estimate that more than half of the animals on Earth live in ((++rainforests cities)).
Even though we already know of more than 30 million animals and plants living in ((++rainforests cities)), there are many more to be discovered.
Rainforests exist all around the world, but they can mainly be found in ((++tropical dry)) regions close to the equator. The orange areas on this map tell you where you can find rainforests.

hint.text: The equator is an imaginary line around the world. This line divides the globe into two hemispheres, or two halves: the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere.
hint.label: Equator

atoms.a: What would it sound like if you were in the rainforest?

instruction.text: Which animals do you expect to see or hear in the rainforest? Select the correct animals.

feedback.correct: This bird is called a keel-billed toucan.
This frog is called a poison dart frog.
This bird is called a crimson-fronted parakeet.
This monkey is called a squirrel monkey.

atoms.b: The name rainforest is not coincidental, as it rains ((++a_lot very_rarely)) in rainforests.
The warm, humid climate is ((++the_perfect not_ideal)) weather for many plants to grow. That is why rainforests are so lush and full of life.
The world’s largest rainforest is in ((++South_America Wales)).

instruction.text: Look at the picture. Select the area where you think there is a rainforest.

correct.text: Well done! This is a map of South America. The dark green area is the biggest rainforest on Earth. It is called the Amazon.

instruction.text: All of these animals live in the Amazon. First, read the description. Then select the correct animal.

atoms.a: I can fly and there is a horn growing out of my forehead.
I like to eat fish and I live in the water.
I live in trees and I love my beard.
I am almost invisible in the darkness.
